memory_update.text: COHR and LITE are the primary reference leaders for direct InP/laser/optical-component exposure in AI datacenter photonics.

AXTI should be tracked as an underfollowed substrate-layer candidate for InP wafer exposure, but survival to later layers depends on verifying AI datacenter customer linkage, backlog quality, and capacity expansion economics.
ALMU belongs only in the speculative shadow lane until commercial qualification, material AI-photonics revenue, and customer evidence are confirmed; financing and dilution risk must be checked.
The node appears to split into three public-market sublayers: established InP/device leaders, substrate/wafer suppliers, and emerging alternative compound-semiconductor integration platforms.
Need a separate pass for equipment and test/measurement enablers around MOCVD, wafer inspection, photonic test, burn-in, and optical transceiver manufacturing services.

AXTI should be carried forward as the main underfollowed public-market candidate for the InP substrate layer; key gating checks are InP revenue mix, export controls, capacity expansion, and customer qualification evidence.
ALMU should remain in the speculative-shadow lane until named commercial AI/datacom customers, qualification status, revenue scale, and dilution risk are verified.
COHR and LITE are not underfollowed but are essential reference anchors for InP laser/device capacity, pricing tightness, and the pace of AI optical interconnect demand.
Need a later pass on non-U.S. substrate and photonics suppliers, plus test/measurement vendors for 800G/1.6T optical qualification, because this pass was constrained to U.S.-listed companies.
Fabrinet is a useful second-order AI optics beneficiary because its value is in manufacturing throughput and optical interconnect assembly, not in headline GPU branding.

The photonics bottleneck may sit in InP wafer/device capacity rather than in the obvious transceiver labels; supplier concentration and qualification cycles are likely more important than broad industry branding.
The most obscure opportunity may be in precision substrates and receive-side devices, where analyst coverage appears thin and qualification cycles can be long.
COHR and LITE should remain reference anchors for the AI photonics/InP device node; they define the commercial qualification and capacity benchmark rather than the underfollowed alpha lane.

AXTI is the strongest underfollowed substrate-level candidate to track for InP/GaAs/Ge wafer exposure, but survival to later layers depends on verified InP revenue, AI/datacenter customer pull, backlog, capacity, and dilution/geopolitical risk.

ALMU belongs in speculative_shadow only: possible III-V-on-silicon alternative platform for photonics scaling, but requires proof of commercial AI/datacom qualification, customer identity, revenue conversion, and cash-runway safety.

Fabrinet is a relevant second-order optical manufacturing beneficiary and should be considered in a separate EMS/precision optical assembly node; it was not included in the four-candidate list because this pass prioritized component/material/device bottlenecks.

node: Photonic components: InP lasers, photodetectors, precision substrates, and compound-semiconductor platforms
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the AI photonics component node. The clearest reference leaders are Coherent and Lumentum because both sit directly in InP, lasers, optical engines, transceivers, and AI data-center optical interconnects. The underfollowed lane adds AXT as a substrate-level candidate tied to InP wafer supply. Aeluma is included only as a speculative shadow candidate because it targets scalable III-V-on-silicon / compound-semiconductor platforms for AI photonics but still requires commercial qualification, revenue scale, customer evidence, and financing-risk verification. Expanded the AI photonic-components node into a two-lane universe. Reference names are Coherent and Lumentum because they are direct InP laser/device capacity anchors for AI optical interconnects. The underfollowed discovery lane is stronger in AXT, a merchant InP/GaAs/Ge substrate supplier with explicit AI optical-transmission exposure and few primary InP substrate suppliers. Aeluma remains a speculative-shadow candidate: it is attempting III-V photonics scaling on larger silicon wafers and has contracts/partners tied to high-speed datacom, but commercial AI qualification and customer evidence remain the key gating items. This node appears to be one of the quieter AI infrastructure chokepoints: direct compound-semiconductor suppliers and photonics manufacturers sit one or two steps away from the obvious GPU story, while qualification cycles, limited supplier counts, and InP capacity constraints may create scarcity.
